text:
Marathon Petroleum jumped 3.7% today as crude oil prices spiked following Saudi Arabia's pipeline closure. The East-West pipeline was damaged in a drone attack and temporarily shut down, pushing U.S. oil to over $105 a barrel—the highest level in recent weeks. When global crude prices rise, refiners like Marathon benefit because they can sell refined products (gasoline, diesel) at higher margins relative to their input costs, especially when refineries are operating at high capacity as they currently are at 97.8%.

The broader Iran-related geopolitical tensions are keeping oil markets elevated. Houthi militants and Iraqi-backed drone strikes on Saudi oil infrastructure have created genuine supply concerns, which is why the U.S. price ($97) remains meaningfully lower than the world price ($109)—the gap reflects fear that more disruptions could hit global supply. This two-week gain of 10% fits the pattern of a refiner benefiting from sustained crude strength driven by Middle East friction rather than any company-specific news.
